name: Dravecor
description: Dravecor is a synthetic catecholamine cascade agent that floods the bloodstream with a precisely calibrated mix of epinephrine analogs and cortisol suppressants, producing a controlled adrenal surge without the cortical fog of raw fight-or-flight response. Lazarus markets it to corporate security contractors and licensed PMCs as a pre-breach compound. The surge hits within ninety seconds of injection and delivers a clean, purposeful aggression — elevated strength output, sharpened tunnel vision, and pain threshold elevation of approximately 40%.
effects: Rapid strength output increase (estimated 35-45% above baseline)
Heightened sensory focus on physical threats
side_effects: Cardiac arrhythmia risk after repeated use
Severe crash — exhaustion and emotional flatness lasting 6-12 hours
Dependency develops within 4-6 weeks of regular use
cultural_context: Dravecor is the workhorse stimulant of corporate security culture — the drug that mid-level enforcers take before raiding a competitor's data floor or protecting a Tier 4 executive convoy. It has enough legitimacy to be carried openly by licensed contractors but enough potency to be coveted on the Shelf. Knockoff versions called 'Grey Surge' are synthesized in Tier 1 labs and are chemically rougher, with a higher cardiac event rate.
story_hooks: A Shelf runner acquires a vial of genuine Dravecor and realizes the batch has a Lazarus internal tracking marker — someone in the supply chain is going to come looking for it.
A corporate security chief has been quietly increasing her team's Dravecor dosage before routine patrols; the arrhythmia deaths are being logged as 'equipment malfunction.'
Grey Surge has started appearing in Tier 2 neighborhoods at prices that make no economic sense — someone is flooding the market deliberately.
